question.prompt: If \(x,\) \(y,\) and \(z\) are real numbers such that \[ \begin{aligned} (x-3)^2+(y-4)^2\\ {}+(z-5)^2&=0, \end{aligned} \] then \(x+y+z=\)

solutions.explanation:
Every square of a real number is nonnegative. If any of the three squared terms were positive, their sum would be positive. Since their sum is zero, all three must be zero:
\[
(x-3)^2=(y-4)^2=(z-5)^2=0.
\]
A square equals zero only when its base is zero, so \(x=3\), \(y=4\), and \(z=5\). These values satisfy the original equation. Hence
\[
x+y+z=3+4+5=12,
\]
choice D.
solutions.title: Use nonnegativity of squares
